questions.prompt: You staged the wrong file but want to keep its working-tree edits. Which command is appropriate?
questions.answer_key: git restore --staged path
questions.explanation: Unstage the file while preserving its working-tree edit.

questions.prompt: Which command creates a new commit that reverses an earlier commit?
questions.answer_key: git revert <commit>
questions.explanation: Revert records a reversing commit; reset moves a reference.

questions.prompt: Which command retrieves remote history without integrating it into the current branch?
questions.answer_key: git fetch origin
questions.explanation: Fetch downloads objects and updates remote-tracking references without automatically merging.

questions.prompt: Why is rebasing published/shared history risky?
options: It can replace commit identities and disrupt collaborators
It permanently makes all files binary
questions.answer_key: It can replace commit identities and disrupt collaborators
questions.explanation: Rebase replays commits and can create new IDs; shared history rewrites require coordination.

questions.prompt: Which command displays recent local reference movements useful during recovery?
questions.answer_key: git reflog
questions.explanation: The reflog records local ref updates; it is not a substitute for a tested backup.

questions.prompt: What does .gitignore do for an already tracked secret file?
options: It does not remove the file from tracked history
It erases the file from every clone
questions.answer_key: It does not remove the file from tracked history
questions.explanation: Revoke/rotate exposed credentials and coordinate history cleanup; ignores only affect untracked paths.

questions.prompt: Which command shows the object type for HEAD?
questions.answer_key: git cat-file -t HEAD
questions.explanation: cat-file is a read-only plumbing command for inspecting Git objects.

questions.prompt: What should precede a potentially destructive cleanup?
options: Preview the target paths and confirm a disposable/backup copy
Assume reflog can restore every untracked file
questions.answer_key: Preview the target paths and confirm a disposable/backup copy
questions.explanation: Many untracked or overwritten files never entered Git history and may be unrecoverable.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between git diff and git diff --cached?
options: Working-tree versus index changes; index versus HEAD changes
questions.answer_key: Working-tree versus index changes; index versus HEAD changes
questions.explanation: The commands inspect different comparisons.

questions.prompt: A push is rejected as non-fast-forward. What is a good next step?
options: Fetch and inspect divergent history before integrating
Immediately use --force on the shared branch
Delete the remote branch without checking
questions.answer_key: Fetch and inspect divergent history before integrating
questions.explanation: Rejection often prevents overwriting remote work.

questions.prompt: What does an annotated tag add beyond a lightweight tag?
options: A tag object with metadata/message and optionally a signature
A separate working tree for a branch
A backup of all untracked files
questions.answer_key: A tag object with metadata/message and optionally a signature
questions.explanation: Annotated tags store a tag object; signatures still require trust checks.

questions.prompt: Why use git bisect?
options: Narrow down which commit introduced a reproducible behavior change
questions.answer_key: Narrow down which commit introduced a reproducible behavior change
questions.explanation: Bisect uses known-good/bad revisions to narrow the search.

questions.prompt: Which Git feature can provide parallel working directories linked to one repository?
questions.answer_key: git worktree
questions.explanation: Worktrees support multiple linked working directories with branch association rules.

questions.prompt: What is required to trust a valid commit signature?
options: Verify key identity and the project’s trust policy separately
Assume any valid signature means author identity is genuine
Store private keys in the repository
questions.answer_key: Verify key identity and the project’s trust policy separately
questions.explanation: Signature validity and trust in key ownership are related but distinct.

questions.prompt: What should a release automation script do when a precondition fails?
options: Stop and report the failing check without continuing destructive steps
Continue and print a warning only
questions.answer_key: Stop and report the failing check without continuing destructive steps
questions.explanation: Automation should use safe defaults, explicit exit-code checks and clear failures.

questions.prompt: Why test a backup by restoring it?
options: To prove that the backup can recreate needed refs/history and is usable
To reduce the repository object count immediately
To grant more contributors write permission
To update a branch without fetching
questions.answer_key: To prove that the backup can recreate needed refs/history and is usable
questions.explanation: A backup process is incomplete until its restore path has been tested.

questions.prompt: What does sparse checkout primarily control?
options: Which tracked paths are present in the working tree
Who can push to a remote
questions.answer_key: Which tracked paths are present in the working tree
questions.explanation: Sparse checkout limits the working-tree subset; files remain tracked in the repository.

questions.prompt: Which step matters if a credential was committed and exposed?
options: Revoke or rotate the credential promptly
questions.answer_key: Revoke or rotate the credential promptly
questions.explanation: History cleanup does not invalidate a leaked credential.

questions.prompt: Why does a commit hash change after amending or rebasing a commit?
options: The commit object metadata/content and/or parent relationship changes
Git uses random IDs every time status is run
The branch name is part of every object id alone
questions.answer_key: The commit object metadata/content and/or parent relationship changes
questions.explanation: Commit IDs identify object contents, including commit metadata and parents.

questions.prompt: Which output is intended to be stable and easy for a script to parse?
options: The default human-readable status prose only
questions.answer_key: git status --porcelain=v1
questions.explanation: Porcelain format is designed for scripts, unlike human-facing output.
